nodes.name: Ru/RuO2/NC hollow nanospheres
nodes.procedure: Initially, dopamine hydrochloride, F-127, and RuCl3 were combined in a water/ethanol solution. A homogeneous nano-emulsion system was created by adding 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (TMB) to the combined solution. Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane solution was used to enhance dopamine polymerization, resulting in Ru/polymerized dopamine (PDA) mesoporous spheres. Finally, Ru/RuO2/NC hollow nanospheres with nitrogen-doped carbon covering were synthesized using stepwise calcination of Ru/PDA precursor in a N2 and air environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru@MWCNT shows favorable HER polarization curve with lower overpotential compared to Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The polarization curves in Figure 2B show the capacity of the catalyst to drive the hydrogen evolution process efficiently, with Ru@MWCNT having a more favorable curve (lower overpotential).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru@C2N exhibits competitive HER activity comparable to Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2D represents the HER performance of multiple catalysts... Ru@C2N exhibits competitive HER activity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/RuO2/NC shows superior ECSA, TOF, and overpotential performance compared to NC and Ru/PDA-N300 as shown in radar plot Figure 3B.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The radar plot in Figure 3B illustrates the HER performance of Ru/RuO2/NC, NC, and Ru/PDA-N300 regarding EIS, TOF, ECSA, and overpotential, demonstrating that Ru/RuO2/NC surpasses the others, especially in TOF, ECSA, and overpotential.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/RuO2/NC exhibits Tafel slope of 39.1 mV dec^-1 indicating enhanced HER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Tafel graphs in Figure 3C indicate that the Ru/RuO2/NC catalyst exhibits a markedly reduced Tafel slope (39.1 mV dec^-1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co/CoxSy@NC-750 shows optimal graphitization at 750°C with distinct D/G peaks and CoxSy presence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the elevation in synthesis temperature, graphitization enhances, seen by the sharpness and heightened intensity of the D and G peaks in Figure 5H.
